business_model.claim: Xeris Biopharma generates commercial revenue in the United States by selling three approved therapies for chronic endocrine and neurological conditions: Recorlev for endogenous hypercortisolemia in Cushing's syndrome, Gvoke for severe hypoglycemia, and Keveyis for primary periodic paralysis.
quotes: We are a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing and commercializing therapies for people with chronic endocrine and neurological diseases in the United States.

We have three commercially available products in the United States: Recorlev, a cortisol synthesis inhibitor for the treatment of endogenous hypercortisolemia in patients with Cushing's syndrome; Gvoke, a ready-to-use liquid glucagon for the treatment of severe hypoglycemia; and Keveyis, a therapy for primary periodic paralysis ("PPP").

business_model.claim: The company sells its commercial products primarily to pharmaceutical wholesalers and specialty pharmacies in the United States for resale to retail pharmacies or patients, while contracting with payors, group purchasing organizations, and healthcare providers for rebates, chargebacks, and discounts.
quotes: We sell product primarily to wholesalers or a specialty pharmacy that subsequently resell to retail pharmacies or patients.

We enter into arrangements with payors, group purchasing organizations, and healthcare providers that provide for government-mandated or privately-negotiated rebates, chargebacks and discounts related to our products.

In addition, our efforts include the support of a single, highly experienced specialty pharmacy that provides logistical assistance in the securing of coverage from third-party payors and then subsequent distribution of Recorlev to patients.

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P3, and P4
business_model.claim: Beyond U.S. product sales, Xeris generates royalty, contract, and other product revenue from formulation collaborations and commercialization partnerships utilizing its proprietary XeriSol and XeriJect non-aqueous delivery platforms.
quotes: Royalty and contract revenue is recognized as earned in accordance with contract terms when it can be reasonably estimated and collectability is reasonably assured.
Revenue generated from various collaboration and technology partnerships are included in this line item.
We are currently collaborating with several major pharmaceutical companies on the development of formulations of their proprietary therapeutics.

quotes: Total revenue was $282.5 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of 37% compared to the same period last year.

business_model.claim: Net product revenue is driven by gross sales volume less estimated allowances for patient copay assistance, prompt payment discounts, government and commercial payor rebates, chargebacks, service fees, and product returns recorded at the time of sale and adjusted as estimates update.
quotes: Product revenue, net, represents gross product sales less estimated allowances for patient copay assistance programs, prompt payment discounts, payor rebates, chargebacks, service fees, and product returns, all of which are recorded at the time of sale to the pharmaceutical wholesaler or other customer.
If actual results differ from our estimates, we make adjustments to these allowances in the period in which the actual results or updates to estimates become known.

business_model.basis: stated in P3, P4, and P6
business_model.claim: Recorlev is the primary revenue growth driver, increasing $75.0 million or 116.7% in 2025 to $139,283 (table in thousands) and reaching 178,088 (table in thousands) in the first nine months of 2026 on higher patient demand, record referrals, and new patient starts after commercial expansion, partly offset in 2025 by $4.6 million or 7.2% of unfavorable net pricing.
quotes: The increase was due to higher volume ($79.6 million or 123.9%), primarily driven by increased patient demand, offset by unfavorable net pricing ($4.6 million or 7.2%).

Net product revenue in the third quarter grew more than 43% year-over-year, led by Recorlev, where our expanded commercial team moved from build to yield and delivered record referrals and new patient starts.

business_model.claim: Gvoke net revenue is driven by net pricing, prescription demand, and gross-to-net adjustments, rising $11.3 million or 13.6% in 2025 to 94,108 (table in thousands) on favorable net pricing ($8.6 million) and higher volume ($2.7 million), while totaling 65,055 (table in thousands) in the first nine months of 2026 as third-quarter back-to-school demand was offset by a one-time ($4 million) gross-to-net adjustment.
quotes: The increase was due to favorable net pricing ($8.6 million or 10.4%) and higher volume ($2.7 million or 3.2%).
which was offset by a one-time ($4 million) gross-to-net adjustment.

business_model.claim: Keveyis revenue reflects net pricing pressure following its August 2022 loss of orphan drug exclusivity and generic competition, declining $1.9 million or 3.8% in 2025 to 47,649 (table in thousands) as unfavorable net pricing ($5.0 million) outweighed higher volume ($3.1 million), before rising to 36,582 (table in thousands) in the first nine months of 2026.
quotes: The decrease was due to unfavorable net pricing ($5.0 million or 10.1%), offset by higher volume ($3.1 million or 6.3%).
In addition, due to the end of orphan drug exclusivity, we expect that additional generic competitors could emerge which may also contribute to the erosion of Keveyis sales.

quotes: We have three commercially available products in the United States: Recorlev, a cortisol synthesis inhibitor for the treatment of endogenous hypercortisolemia in patients with Cushing's syndrome; Gvoke, a ready-to-use liquid glucagon for the treatment of severe hypoglycemia; and Keveyis, a therapy for primary periodic paralysis ("PPP").

competitive_position.claim: Recorlev holds U.S. orphan drug exclusivity through December 30, 2028, FDA Orange Book-listed U.S. patents providing protection through 2040, and a commercial model utilizing CareConnection support and a single specialty pharmacy.
quotes: Recorlev has received orphan drug exclusivity status in the United States through December 30, 2028 and patent protection through 2040.

In addition, our efforts include the support of a single, highly experienced specialty pharmacy that provides logistical assistance in the securing of coverage from third-party payors and then subsequent distribution of Recorlev to patients.

Included in the total patents, we have 70 granted patents globally related to our platform technologies and nine patents granted in the United States and listed in the FDA Orange Book covering proprietary formulations of levoketoconazole (the active pharmaceutical ingredient in Recorlev) and the uses of such formulations in treating certain endocrine-related diseases and syndromes.

quotes: Net revenue increased by $75.0 million or 116.7% for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to the year ended December 31, 2024.

Net product revenue in the third quarter grew more than 43% year-over-year, led by Recorlev, where our expanded commercial team moved from build to yield and delivered record referrals and new patient starts.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 and Item 1A Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: Recorlev faces competition from established Cushing's syndrome therapies—including Corcept Therapeutics' Korlym, Recordati's Signifor LAR and Isturisa, and older generic drugs such as ketoconazole used off-label—and from Corcept's Phase 3 candidate relacorilant.
quotes: Recorlev competes primarily with other established medications and therapies, including older generic drugs that are used off-label for Recorlev's approved indication.

To our knowledge, the products used for the treatment of endogenous Cushing's syndrome patients who fail or are ineligible for surgery in the United States and Europe are: Korlym (mifepristone) marketed by Corcept Therapeutics in the United States; Signifor LAR (pasireotide) and Isturisa (osilodrostat), both marketed by Recordati in the United States and European Union ("EU"); and ketoconazole, metyrapone and mitotane marketed by HRA in the EU.
Corcept is developing relacorilant, a second-generation glucocorticoid receptor modulator; currently in Phase 3.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Item 2 Patent Rights.
competitive_position.claim: Gvoke holds patent protection through 2036 and addresses an estimated U.S. market of more than 14 million at-risk diabetes patients, of whom approximately 1 million are currently protected.
quotes: Gvoke has patent protection through 2036.

There are more than 14 million people with diabetes taking insulin or insulin secretagogues in the United States, and as such, are at-risk and should be prescribed and have handy, a ready-to-use rescue glucagon, like the Gvoke HypoPen for use during a potential severe hypoglycemic episode.

Current prescription volumes suggest that approximately 1 million people with diabetes are adequately protected today, leaving a significant number of people without protection as recommended by the latest guidelines.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 and Item 1A, Q3 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A, and Q3 2026 Form 8-K.
competitive_position.claim: Gvoke competes against multiple marketed severe hypoglycemia therapies—including Baqsimi, Zegalogue, GlucaGen HypoKit, Fresenius Kabi's emergency kit, and Amphastar's generic glucagon—amid still-limited awareness and a decline in net revenue from 69,463 (table in thousands) to 65,055 (table in thousands) in the nine months ended September 30, 2026.
quotes: Gvoke has numerous competitors in the severe hypoglycemia market, which currently include Amphastar’s Baqsimi, an intranasal glucagon dry powder, Zealand Pharma’s Zegalogue, a dasiglucagon outlicensed to Novo Nordisk, Novo Nordisk’s GlucaGen HypoKit, Fresenius Kabi's glucagon emergency kit for low blood sugar, and Amphastar’s generic Glucagon for Injection Emergency Kit.

The marketplace for Gvoke and other ready-to-use glucagon products is significant, owing to the widespread and growing prevalence of diabetes, the large proportion of people with diabetes at risk of experiencing a severe hypoglycemic event, and the still limited awareness of the availability of innovative, ready-to-use glucagon.
Gvoke delivered stronger-than-historical back-to-school prescription demand in the third quarter, which was offset by a one-time ($4 million) gross-to-net adjustment.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1, Q3 2026 Form 10-Q, Q3 2026 Form 8-K, and October 14, 2026 Form 8-K.
competitive_position.claim: Keveyis is an FDA-approved therapy for primary periodic paralysis backed by proprietary patient-identification analytics and a specialty pharmacy, and Xeris received U.S. Patent No. 12,758,502 in October 2026 and sued generic sellers for infringement.
quotes: Keveyis is the first therapy approved in the United States to treat hyperkalemic, hypokalemic, and related variants of PPP.
To address this, we have built an extensive set of patient support processes and proprietary analytics to identify patients affected by PPP and suitable for Keveyis therapy treatment.

On October 13, 2026, Xeris Biopharma Holdings, Inc. (the “Company”), through its wholly owned subsidiary, Xeris Pharmaceuticals, Inc., filed patent infringement lawsuits in the United States District Court for the District of New Jersey against defendants (i) Torrent Pharma Inc., Torrent Pharmaceuticals Limited, Cycle Pharmaceuticals Limited, Lemed Pharmacy III, LLC, and Lemed Specialty Pharmacy Arizona, LLC; and (ii) Rising Pharma Holdings, Inc. and Rising Pharma Specialties Pvt. Ltd. in two separate actions.
These lawsuits were filed following the grant of U.S. Patent No. 12,758,502 (the “’502 patent”) related to the Company’s KEVEYIS® (dichlorphenamide) product.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Items 1, 1A, and 7, and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A.
competitive_position.claim: Keveyis lost orphan drug exclusivity on August 7, 2022, faces FDA-approved generic dichlorphenamide competitors including Torrent's generic and Cycle Pharmaceuticals' Ormalvi alongside off-label therapies, and saw net revenue fall $1.9 million or 3.8% in 2025 due to unfavorable net pricing.
quotes: Keveyis (dichlorphenamide) is an oral carbonic anhydrase inhibitor that was approved in the United States to treat hyperkalemic, hypokalemic, and related variants of PPP for which orphan drug exclusivity ended on August 7, 2022.
Torrent's ANDA for generic dichlorphenamide was approved on December 29, 2022 and now competes with Keveyis, which may adversely impact our revenue.
In May 2024, Torrent partnered with Cycle Pharmaceuticals to launch Ormalvi, a branded generic version of our Keveyis product.
Net revenue decreased by $1.9 million or 3.8% for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to the year ended December 31, 2024.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Item 2.
competitive_position.claim: As of October 30, 2026, Xeris owned 197 issued patents globally—including 70 global platform patents—covering its non-aqueous XeriSol and XeriJect formulation technologies used in commercial products, pipeline programs, and collaborations with major pharmaceutical companies.
quotes: As of October 30, 2026, we owned 197 patents issued globally, including composition of matter patents covering our ready-to-use glucagon formulation that expire in 2036.

Our proprietary non-aqueous XeriSol and XeriJect technologies offer the opportunity to eliminate the need for reconstitution and refrigeration, enable long-term stability, significantly reduce injection volume, and allow for a more convenient SC or IM administration as opposed to IV infusion and other routes of administration.
We are currently collaborating with several major pharmaceutical companies on the development of formulations of their proprietary therapeutics.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Items 1 and 1A and Q3 2026 Form 8-K.
competitive_position.claim: Xeris's Phase 3-ready pipeline candidate XP-8121 targets hypothyroidism as a once-weekly subcutaneous levothyroxine injection with U.S. Patent No. 12,751,937 expected to expire on October 19, 2043, though it faces inherent clinical development and regulatory risks.
quotes: XP-8121 is designed to be a once-weekly, small-volume, subcutaneous injection that, given its route of administration, bypasses the gastrointestinal tract and could avoid many of the therapeutic complications associated with the use of oral forms of levothyroxine.

On October 6, 2026, the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) granted Xeris U.S. Patent No. 12,751,937, entitled “Stable Levothyroxine Compositions In Aprotic Polar Solvents,” which is expected to expire on October 19, 2043.
Xeris remains on track to initiate Cornerstone by year-end 2026, with topline data expected in late 2028 and potential approval and launch in 2030.
Our product candidates are in various stages of development and subject to the risks of failure inherent in developing drug products.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors and Item 7 MD&A, and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Balance Sheet.
competitive_position.claim: Xeris faces major pharmaceutical competitors with substantially greater financial, technical, manufacturing, and marketing resources, while commercial success depends on third-party payor reimbursement, rebates, and avoiding adverse comparative effectiveness research.
quotes: Many of our current and potential competitors are major pharmaceutical companies that have substantially greater financial, technical, manufacturing and marketing resources than we do, and they may succeed in developing or marketing products that would render our products obsolete or noncompetitive.

In addition, in the United States, the federal government provides funding for comparative effectiveness research, which may compare our products with other treatments and may result in published findings that would, in turn, discourage use of our products by physicians, patients and third-party payors.
